extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent applicants, IP practitioners, rights holders, collective management organizations, and Vietnamese government agencies responsible for IP
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory criteria and procedural requirements from the Vietnamese law text covering copyright/related rights and industrial property (inventions, designs, layout-designs, marks, trade names). Useful for assessing eligibility, exclusions, registration requirements, durations, and infringement acts under Vietnam IP law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive rights of broadcasting organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcasting organizations shall have the exclusive right to exercise or authorize others to: (a) broadcast or rebroadcast their broadcasts; (b) distribute to the public their broadcasts; (c) fix their broadcasts; (d) reproduce their fixed broadcasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcasting organizations also 'shall enjoy material benefits when their broadcasts are recorded and distributed to the public.' (Art.31)

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases where permission and payment are not required (related rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses of related rights where permission and payment are not required include: (a) duplication of works by authors for scientific research; (b) duplication by authors for teaching, except for certain published performances/phonograms/video recordings/broadcasts made for teaching; (c) reasonable recitation for informatory purpose; (d) making provisional copies by broadcasting organizations themselves for broadcasting when they enjoy the broadcasting right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations/individuals using these exemptions must neither affect normal utilization nor cause prejudice to the rights of performers, producers of phonograms/video recordings, and broadcasting organizations. (Art.32)

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases where permission is not required but payment is required (related rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations/individuals need not seek permission but must pay agreed royalties/remunerations when: (a) they directly or indirectly use already-published phonograms or video recordings in broadcasts that are sponsored, advertised or charged in any form; (b) they use already-published phonograms or video recordings in business or commercial activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users under this clause must not affect normal utilization or prejudice the rights of performers/producers/broadcasting organizations. (Art.33)

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of related-right protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Performers' rights: 50 years from year following fixation; producers of phonograms/video recordings: 50 years from year following publication, or 50 years from year following fixation for unpublished phonograms/video recordings; broadcasting organizations: 50 years from year following making of the broadcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms expire at 24:00 hrs of December 31 of the year of expiration. (Art.34)

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts constituting infringement of related rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated infringing acts include appropriating rights of performers/producers/broadcasting orgs; impersonation; publishing/producing/distributing fixed performances/phonograms/video recordings/broadcasts without permission; modifying/distorting performances prejudicial to honor; copying/reciting fixed works without permission; disengaging/modifying electronic right management information; canceling/deactivating technical protection measures; publishing/distributing/importing copies when knowing RM info was altered; manufacturing/selling equipment knowingly aiding illegal decoding of encrypted satellite signals; knowingly receiving/relaying encrypted satellite signals encoded without permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List is a non-exhaustive enumeration of infringing acts used to determine violations and enforcement. (Art.35)

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of copyright/related rights (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment means transfer by copyright/related-rights holders of ownership of specified economic/moral rights to others under contract or law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must not assign moral rights (except right of publication); performers must not assign certain moral rights. Joint ownership requires agreement of all co-owners for assignment; separate detachable parts may be assigned separately. (Art.45)

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of assignment contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright/related-rights assignment contract must be in writing and include: (a) names and addresses of assignor and assignee; (b) assignment bases; (c) payment price and mode; (d) rights and obligations of parties; (e) liability for breaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance, amendment, termination, or cancellation of such contracts shall comply with Civil Code provisions. (Art.46)

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing of copyright/related rights (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensing is permission by holders for others to use for a definite term one, several or all specified rights. Authors/performers must not license certain moral rights (exceptions apply). Joint ownership requires agreement of all co-owners; detachable parts may be licensed separately. Licensees may sublicense with permission of right holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines licensing as a distinct mode of exploiting rights with limits on moral rights and joint-ownership rules. (Art.47)

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of license contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright/related-rights license contract must be in writing and include: (a) full names and addresses of licensor and licensee; (b) licensing bases; (c) licensing scope; (d) payment price and mode; (e) rights and obligations of parties; (f) liability for breaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance, amendment, termination or cancellation of license contracts must comply with the Civil Code. (Art.48)

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of copyright/related rights (purpose and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration is filing applications/dossiers with competent state agencies to record information on authors/works/copyright/related-rights holders. Registration is not compulsory for enjoyment of rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holders granted certificates do not bear burden of proof of such rights in disputes unless rebutting proof is adduced. (Art.49)

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents for registration
rubrics_metrics.description: An application comprises: (a) a written declaration for registration (in Vietnamese, signed, with applicant/author/holder info, summarized content, derivative-work info if applicable, date/place/form of publication, responsibility guarantee); (b) two copies of the work or fixed object; (c) letter of authorization if applicant is authorized person; (d) documents proving right to file if via inheritance/assignment; (e) written consent of co-authors for joint works; (f) written consent of co-owners for joint-ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents c/d/e/f must be in Vietnamese; foreign documents must be translated. The Culture and Information Ministry sets the form of written declarations. (Art.50)

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence to grant registered copyright/related-rights certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The state management agency in charge of copyright and related rights is competent to grant registered copyright and related-rights certificates, and can re-grant, renew or revoke such certificates. Government specifies conditions, order, and procedures for these acts; the Culture and Information Ministry sets certificate forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegates administrative competence and rulemaking on certificates. (Art.51)

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for granting registered certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Within fifteen working days after receipt of a valid dossier, the competent state agency shall grant the certificate or notify in writing the refusal to grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to registered copyright or registered related-rights certificates. (Art.52)

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity and territorial scope of registered certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered copyright and related-rights certificates are valid throughout the Vietnamese territory. Certificates granted before the law's effective date continue to be valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies territorial validity and grandfathering of earlier certificates. (Art.53)

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and publication of registered certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered certificates shall be recorded in the national register of copyright and related rights. Decisions on grant, re-grant, renewal or revocation shall be published in the Official Gazette on copyright and related rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures public record and transparency of administrative decisions. (Art.54)

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-grant, renewal, and revocation of registered certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency shall re-grant/renew certificates if lost/damaged or holder changed. Agency shall revoke certificates where grantee is not the author/holder or where the subject is ineligible for protection. Third parties may request revocation where grant is contrary to the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides grounds and parties entitled to request administrative revocation. (Art.55)

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective rights management organizations: status and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Collective representative organizations are non-profit organizations established by agreement among authors/copyright/related-rights holders to operate per law; they may manage rights, negotiate licensing/collection/division of royalties, protect members' legitimate interests, and organize conciliations in disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They shall conduct creation-promoting activities, cooperate with national/international counterparts, report to competent state agencies, and perform other duties under law. (Art.56)

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and related-rights consultancy/service organizations: functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Such organizations operate under law and, at request of authors/holders, provide consultancy on legal issues, carry out registration procedures on behalf of holders under authorization, and join other legal relations regarding rights protection under authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines permissible support activities these entities may provide. (Art.57)

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention patent protection conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be protected by grant of an invention patent when it satisfies: (a) being novel; (b) involving an inventive step; (c) being susceptible of industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the three-part patentability test for inventions. (Art.58(1))

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility solution patent protection conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility solution patent protects an invention that, unless common knowledge, satisfies: (a) being novel; (b) being susceptible of industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility solution patents do not require an inventive step. (Art.58(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matters not protected as inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Not protected: (1) scientific discoveries/theories, mathematical methods; (2) schemes/plans/rules/methods for mental acts, training animals, games, business; computer programs; (3) presentations of information; (4) solutions of aesthetic characteristics only; (5) plant varieties, animal breeds; (6) plant/animal production processes principally biological other than microbiological; (7) human and animal disease prevention, diagnostic and treatment methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates categories excluded from patent protection. (Art.59)

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of inventions (general definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is novel if it has not been publicly disclosed through use or written description or any other form, inside or outside the country, before the filing date or priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy among a limited number of persons obliged to keep it secret does not count as public disclosure. (Art.60(1)-(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty exceptions/grace period for inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention does not lose novelty if published in these cases, provided application is filed within 6 months from date of publication: (a) published by another person without permission of right-to-register person; (b) published as a scientific presentation by the right-to-register person; (c) displayed at a national exhibition of Vietnam or an officially recognized international exhibition by the right-to-register person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides limited grace period and specific exceptional circumstances preserving novelty. (Art.60(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention involves an inventive step if, based on technical solutions already publicly disclosed prior to filing/priority date, it constitutes inventive progress and cannot be easily created by a person with average knowledge in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'person having average knowledge in the art' (person skilled in the art) is the comparative standard to assess obviousness. (Art.61)

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability of inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is susceptible of industrial application if it is possible to realize mass manufacture/production of products or repeated application of the process and to achieve stable results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires practical, repeatable application and stable outcomes. (Art.62)

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design protection conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design shall be protected when it satisfies: (1) being new; (2) being creative; (3) being susceptible of industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-part test analogous to invention test but using 'creative' rather than 'inventive step'. (Art.63)

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matters not protected as industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Not protected: (1) product appearance dictated by technical features; (2) appearance of civil/industrial construction works; (3) shape invisible during product use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits design protection where appearance is purely functional or not visible. (Art.64)

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design is new if it significantly differs from other industrial designs publicly disclosed prior to filing/priority date. Two designs are not significantly different if differences are only in appearance features that are not easily noticeable and memorable and cannot distinguish the designs as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy among limited persons counts as not publicly disclosed. A 6‑month grace period applies (file within 6 months) for publication by others without permission, scientific presentation by right-to-register person, or display at national/official exhibitions. (Art.65)

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity of industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design is creative if, based on industrial designs already publicly disclosed before filing/priority date, it cannot be easily created by a person with average knowledge in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous 'non-obviousness' threshold for designs measured against the skilled designer. (Art.66)

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability of industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design is susceptible of industrial application if it can be used as a model for mass manufacture of products with appearance embodying the design by industrial or handicraft methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires the design be producible at scale by industrial or craft methods. (Art.67)

rubrics_metrics.name: Layout-design protection conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A layout-design shall be protected when it satisfies: (1) being original; (2) being commercially novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets dual originality and commercial novelty thresholds for semiconductor layout-designs. (Art.68)

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matters not protected as layout-designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Not protected: (1) principles, processes, systems or methods operated by semiconductor integrated circuits; (2) information or software contained in semiconductor integrated circuits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excludes functional/process/software subject matter from layout-design protection. (Art.69)

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of layout-designs
rubrics_metrics.description: A layout-design is original if: (a) it is the result of its author's creative labor; (b) it was not widely known among creators of layout-designs or manufacturers of semiconductor ICs at creation time. A combination of common elements/interconnections is original only if the combination as a whole is original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both authorship/creativity and novelty among peers are required; combinations are assessed as a whole. (Art.70)

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial novelty of layout-designs
rubrics_metrics.description: A layout-design is commercially novel if it has not been commercially exploited anywhere in the world prior to filing. It does not lose commercial novelty if the application is filed within 2 years from first commercial exploitation anywhere by the person entitled to register it or their licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial exploitation is public distribution for commercial purposes of an IC produced by incorporating the layout-design, or a commodity containing such IC; provides a 2‑year grace for the rights-holder's own first exploitation. (Art.71)

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark protection general conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A mark shall be protected when it: (1) is a visible sign (letters/words/drawings/images/holograms or combinations, in one or more colors); (2) is capable of distinguishing the owner's goods/services from those of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes visibility and distinctiveness as core registration requirements. (Art.72)

rubrics_metrics.name: Signs not protected as marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs not protected include: (1) signs identical or confusingly similar to national flags/emblems; (2) signs identical/confusingly similar to emblems/names of Vietnamese state/political/socio-political organizations or international organizations unless permitted; (3) signs identical/confusingly similar to real names/aliases/images of leaders/heroes/famous personalities; (4) signs identical/confusingly similar to certification/check/warranty seals of international orgs unless registered as certification marks; (5) signs that mislead or deceive consumers as to origin, properties, intended utilities, quality, value or other characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates absolute and relative exclusions protecting public symbols, personalities, certification marks, and preventing consumer deception. (Art.73)

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness and non-distinctiveness of marks
rubrics_metrics.description: A mark is distinctive if it consists of one or several easily noticeable and memorable elements or a combination forming such; a mark is indistinctive if it falls into listed cases including simple shapes, numerals/letters, conventional signs, descriptive signs indicating category/quality/utility, signs indicating legal status or business field, geographic indications (unless acquired distinctiveness), signs identical/similar to earlier-filed/registered marks or widely used marks, marks identical/similar to registered well-known marks, trade names in use causing confusion, or insignificantly different from protected industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains a detailed multi-point list (a–m) of circumstances that render a mark indistinctive, including acquired distinctiveness exceptions and rules about prior registrations/recognition. (Art.74)

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for evaluation of well-known marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors to consider when determining well-known status: (1) number of consumers aware of the mark via purchase/use/advertising; (2) territorial area of circulation; (3) turnover/quantity sold or services provided; (4) duration of continuous use; (5) wide reputation of goods/services; (6) number of countries protecting the mark; (7) number of countries recognizing the mark as well-known; (8) assignment price/licensing price/investment capital contribution value of the mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides quantitative and qualitative indicia used in administrative/judicial assessment of well-known mark status. (Art.75)

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade name protection general condition
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade name shall be protected when it is capable of distinguishing the business entity bearing it from other business entities operating in the same business field and locality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on distinctiveness within same field/locality as the protective threshold. (Art.76)

rubrics_metrics.name: Names not protected as trade names
rubrics_metrics.description: Names of state agencies, political organizations, socio-political organizations, socio-political-professional organizations, social organizations, socio-professional organizations or other entities that are not involved in business activities shall not be protected as trade names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents non-commercial/public entities' names from gaining trade-name protection. (Art.77)

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness of trade names
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade name is distinctive when it: (1) consists of a proper name, except where it has been widely known through use; (2) is not identical with or confusingly similar to a trade name used earlier by another person in same business field/locality; (3) is not identical with or confusingly similar to another person's mark or protected geographical indication used earlier than its use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets rules preventing consumer confusion and respecting prior marks/geographical indications. (Art.78)
